correctness.rationale: The characteristic-two discriminant is H² with H=a²d²+ab²e+abcd+bce+c²d+e²; U=e+ad,V=c+ab gives H=U²+bUV+dV², primitive linear in d, hence integral. Partial derivatives give Jacobian (U²,UV,V²,bU,bV)=(U,V)∩(b,(U,V)²), radical (U,V) and embedded prime (b,U,V). S=k[a,b,R,V] with d=R²+bR,U=RV is finite birational integrally closed normalization. S/B has one P=k[a,b,d]-module generator R killed by (U,V), proving conductor. F_q counts q4 for Y and q3 for Z. Independent characteristic-two coordinate expansion and q2/q4 checks corroborate finite cases without proving the normalization.
